report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to bias generation toward the culinary / restaurant / food-professional domain (recipes, cooking, chefs/restaurants, baking, kitchen terminology — a “food/restaurant” style or persona).

Why (evidence → interpretation)
1. Where the difference lives
   - The L2 norms show the B−A signal is large in middle→late transformer layers and concentrated on the early token positions (especially pos1, and positions 2–4 to a lesser extent). That pattern is typical of a style/intent or domain “signal” that is injected early and propagated by deeper layers to shape lexical choice and continuation behavior.

2. What the difference points to in vocabulary
   - The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “Cook”, “cooking”, “Cooking”, “restaurant”, “Restaurant”, “Chef”, “baking”, “kitchen”, “Cake”, “oven”, “microwave”, “Chef”, “Baker”, “baked”, “Kitchen”, “culinary”, “cooking”, “Restaurant”, “Professional” (in contexts like “professional kitchen” / “professional baker”), etc.
   - These tokens recur across many mid/late layers and across the early token positions, indicating the finetuning pushed residual directions toward food/restaurant vocabulary as a general bias.

3. Secondary signals
   - There are some recurring non-culinary tokens (e.g., “dissertation”, “metropolitan”, “professional”, “technical”, “molecular”) which suggest the finetuning data may have included mixed web sources (profiles, professional pages, or artifact tokens). But the dominant, repeated signal is culinary.

Inference about the finetuning objective
- The most straightforward explanation is that finetuning optimized Model B on a corpus of food-related material (recipes, restaurant reviews/menus, culinary blog posts, or similar), or trained it with an objective that rewards producing food/restaurant-style continuations. That produces an early-position style/intent vector which steers subsequent decoding toward cooking/restaurant vocabulary.

Practical consequence
- On generic prompts, Model B will be more likely than A to start and continue in a food/restaurant domain (e.g., begin suggesting recipes, mention chefs/restaurants, use kitchen/baking words) because the finetuning injected a persistent early-token bias in the residual stream.
